solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Great old bovine pleasure-seeker

parts.note: great in the sense of grand or heroic, as in an epic achievement
the urus is the aurochs, an extinct wild ox

explanation.surface: A huge prehistoric ox is cast as a hedonist chasing its own enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: The URUS (aurochs) is a crossword regular for 'old ox' or 'old bovine'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek philosopher who taught that pleasure is the highest good; his name now stands for a lover of the good life.

clue.text: Kind of dash by recruit or officer

parts.note: an en dash is the printer's mid-length dash, named for the width of a letter n
to recruit someone is to sign them up

explanation.surface: A dash of some sort is drawn by a new soldier or by their superior.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior commissioned rank, historically the infantry officer who carried the regimental colours.

clue.text: Book's account, one that's surprising

parts.note: an ISA is an Individual Savings Account, a tax-free British savings account
the Roman numeral for one
an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A book's story is said to contain someone who surprises.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA (Individual Savings Account) is a UK tax-free savings product. The 's after 'Book' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophetic book of the Old Testament, named after the prophet who wrote it.

clue.text: Guide to form true with these

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are put together to form something new, a shuffle

explanation.surface: A set of instructions on how to make 'true' using these.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to form' signals that TRUE and THESE are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinema attendant shows patrons to their seats with a torch, so she is a guide.

clue.text: Vain academic welcomed by college board

indicators.note: one piece is welcomed into the other, so it goes inside it

parts.note: uni is short for university, here standing for college
prof is short for professor
a board is a table, as in bed and board or a board meeting

explanation.surface: A conceited don is received by the governing body of a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vain' is not conceited here but futile, as in 'in vain'; 'board' is a table, as in bed and board.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort in vain brings no return or benefit, so it is fruitless and without gain.

clue.text: Maybe shanty hasn't finished in time

indicators.note: the phrase loses its final letter, as if it did not reach its end

parts.note: a shanty is an example of a sea song, sung by sailors

explanation.surface: A sailors' work song breaks off before its last verse is sung in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't finished' cuts the last letter G from SEA SONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of the year such as summer, or a stretch like the holiday period, is a span of time.

clue.text: Provide banter for surfers?

parts.note: internet surfers live online, and the prefix e- marks something electronic
a quip is a piece of witty banter

explanation.surface: Supplying jokes for people riding the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: The surfers are web surfers, not wave riders: their banter would be an electronic quip, an e-quip.
explanation.definitionFit: To kit someone out with what they need is to supply or furnish them.

clue.text: Aunt Sally's blemishes brought up by bishop, say

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing a word up means reading it from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: warts are skin blemishes
a bishop is an example of a chessman, or man

explanation.surface: A relative's skin flaws are mentioned by a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally is a traditional British pub game in which sticks are thrown at a dummy's head; figuratively a target set up to be knocked down. 'brought up' turns WARTS into STRAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean an easy target or a weak argument set up only to be knocked down.

clue.text: Officially attest this implies pay will be no better

definitions.meaning: to certify a document formally before a legal official

definitions.text: this implies pay will be no better
definitions.meaning: split as three words plus one, the answer says the pay award is no increase

explanation.surface: A formal certification that wages are frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as NOT A RISE: no better pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary is the legal official who witnesses and certifies signatures, so the verb means to certify formally.

clue.text: Phaeton's alternative for this?

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of the letters of the word gives a different word

explanation.surface: Asking what could replace a phaeton, an open horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' rearranges the letters of PHAETONS. The whole clue also defines: a phaeton and a stanhope are both light open carriages, so one is an alternative for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A light open one-seated carriage, named after the clergyman for whom it was first built, could replace a phaeton.

clue.text: Keep feature some reporter ruthlessly rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters are read backwards
only some of the letters of the phrase are used, a run within it

explanation.surface: A journalist is coldly turned down over a story's feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes TERRUT from inside 'reporter ruthlessly'; 'rejected' turns it round. 'Keep' is the castle stronghold, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tower projecting from a castle wall is a typical part of a castle's main tower or stronghold.

clue.text: Leave monster concealed in famous mount

parts.note: to desert is to leave or abandon
an orc is a goblin-like monster, as in Tolkien
hid means concealed

explanation.surface: Abandon a beast hidden inside a celebrated horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert Orchid was a much-loved grey British steeplechaser, winner of the Cheltenham Gold Cup in 1989.
explanation.definitionFit: A mount is a horse that is ridden, and this was a celebrated racehorse.

clue.text: We're told to look angrily for egg white

indicators.note: what we are told we hear spoken, so the sound of a word stands in for it

parts.note: to glare is to stare angrily

explanation.surface: Instructions to scowl at the white of an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A glaze made from beaten white of egg, used in bookbinding and gilding.

clue.text: Heading for victory, were poor moves to create defeat?

indicators.note: the letters move about into a new order
the head, or first letter, of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A team bound for victory plays badly yet somehow wins?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading for' gives V from 'victory'; 'moves' rearranges V with WERE POOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcome an opponent by superior force is to beat or subdue them.

clue.text: Planned designs, with atlas showing decorative feature

indicators.note: the letters are planned out, laid out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Carefully worked-out patterns, along with a book of maps, make an ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planned' rearranges the letters of DESIGNS and ATLAS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured glass set in windows, as in churches, is an ornamental element of a building.

clue.text: Love big and small changes in worldview?

indicators.note: the combined letters change into a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like O

explanation.surface: Wondering whether love, large and small, shifts how one sees the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges O (love, nil in tennis) with BIG and SMALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy or outlook that treats the whole planet as the proper sphere for economics and politics is a world-wide perspective.

clue.text: Fancy dispensing with US alcohol range

indicators.note: the named letters are done without, taken out of the word

parts.note: to fancy is to suspect or suppose
rum is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: An elaborate drink with no American element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' is the verb (I fancy he's right), giving SUSPECT; 'dispensing with' removes US, leaving SPECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A full span of colours, opinions or options is a broad range.

clue.text: American writer with half-hearted work, one ruminates

parts.note: Gertrude Stein, the American author

indicators.note: the heart of the word is its middle pair of letters, and half of them is lost

parts.note: a book is a written work

explanation.surface: A US author produces a lukewarm piece of writing and then ponders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one of the two middle letters O of BOOK. 'one ruminates' looks like a thinker but means an animal that chews the cud.
explanation.definitionFit: A small African antelope, which like all antelopes chews the cud, is a ruminant.

clue.text: Rot expressed about intriguing people

parts.note: to put something is to express it, as in 'to put it mildly'
re means about or concerning
a faction is a plotting group within a party

explanation.surface: Nonsense was said about a scheming clique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rot' looks like nonsense but is decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Decomposition of organic matter is rotting or decay.

clue.text: Burnt meat stored in empty fridge

indicators.note: the piece is stored inside the other, put within it
an emptied word keeps only its outside letters, the contents gone

parts.note: lamb is a kind of meat

explanation.surface: Charred meat kept in a fridge that has nothing else in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves the outer letters F and E of 'fridge'; 'stored in' puts LAMB between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Food served with brandy set alight has been set on fire, a culinary sense of burnt.

clue.text: Bearing case, abandoning home

indicators.note: the named letters are abandoned, left out of the word

parts.note: an instance is a case or example
in means at home

explanation.surface: A legal case being given up by someone leaving home.
explanation.definitionFit: Posture or the way one stands is one's carriage or bearing.

clue.text: Sharp character from abroad, a tradesman

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a foreign character
a seller is someone who trades goods

explanation.surface: A shrewd foreign person who works in a trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp' is the noun, a cheat or sharper, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler or cheat is a sharp, as in a card sharp.

clue.text: Note penetrating conclusion is correct

indicators.note: one piece penetrates the other, going inside it

parts.note: the end is the conclusion
me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A sharp remark at the finish is accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' is the sol-fa note, not a written message; 'penetrating' signals that it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct its errors.

clue.text: Award frequently picked up

indicators.note: what is picked up by the ear is heard, so the sound stands for the spelling

parts.note: frequently means a lot, often

explanation.surface: A prize that is often collected.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to give out or assign a share, to grant.

clue.text: Bachelor enters dressed or stripped

indicators.note: the letter enters the other word, going inside it

parts.note: robed means dressed in robes
B is the abbreviation for Bachelor, as in BA

explanation.surface: A single man walks in either clothed or naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed' and 'stripped' look like opposites in one surface; only 'stripped' defines, in the sense of plundered.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripped of one's goods means plundered or deprived.

clue.text: Person in charge locks maiden in gaol

indicators.note: the pieces are placed in the other one

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
locks are hair
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: The boss shuts a young woman up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' looks like a verb (locks up) but is hair; a maiden over in cricket is one with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: The one who presides over a meeting or company is its head.

clue.text: Deposing Liberal, exploit trouble for national leader

indicators.note: the party is deposed, removed from the word

parts.note: to milk something is to exploit it
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: After the Liberals are ousted, the new head of state makes the most of the turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposing' takes L out of MILK, leaving MIK.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic title of the Emperor of Japan, the head of that nation.

clue.text: Novel's plot comprehended by a lady

indicators.note: the piece is comprehended, taken in, by the others, so sits inside them

parts.note: a dame is a lady
a bed is a plot in a garden

explanation.surface: A noblewoman grasps a book's storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a storyline but is a flower bed; it goes inside A DAME.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's first novel, published in 1859, is named after its carpenter hero.
